issues.description: Silent failure when arch cannot be extracted from URL produces malformed koji URL
issues.detail: extract_arch_from_url returns None on no match, but use_koji_url_only uses it via f-string, producing '.../latest/None/Packages/...'. This will silently generate a bad URL rather than failing loudly. Should raise an exception or log+skip when arch is unparseable so issues surface immediately in CI.

issues.description: First-character subdirectory derivation breaks for NEVRAs starting with non-alphanumeric or capitalized names
issues.detail: nevra[0].lower() assumes koji's pool directory layout uses the first lowercase letter of the filename. While most package names are lowercase, the koji pool structure actually uses the package name's first char (not NEVRA filename first char). For packages whose RPM filename begins differently than expected (e.g., numeric prefixes), this could produce a 404.

issues.description: Race condition between bump-lockfile merge and koji tagging is acknowledged but not mitigated
issues.detail: The PR description admits a race between writing the lockfile and coreos-koji-tagger making URLs valid. There is no retry, verification, or HEAD check on the constructed URL before writing it to rpms.lock.yaml. Konflux builds that fire before tagging completes will fail to fetch, with no diagnostic pointing back here.

issues.description: Hardcoded arch list duplicates knowledge already available elsewhere
issues.detail: The arches list ['x86_64', 'aarch64', 'ppc64le', 's390x'] is hardcoded in extract_arch_from_url. The script already imports get_basearch from cosalib and iterates over arches in generate_main. Passing the known arch in (or using a module-level constant shared with the caller) avoids drift when new arches are added.

issues.description: Arch regex can match within a NEVRA token, not just path segments
issues.detail: The \b word-boundary regex will match 'x86_64' anywhere in the URL string, including in the rpm filename itself (e.g., a package literally named with an arch substring). For typical fedora URLs this is fine, but extracting arch from the path component would be more robust than searching the full URL.

issues.description: Dead code path: query_packages_location still prioritizes coreos-pool URLs that are then overwritten
issues.detail: The retained coreos-pool prioritization in query_packages_location becomes partially redundant now that use_koji_url_only rewrites all non-coreos-pool URLs anyway. Worth a comment clarifying why the prioritization still matters (preferring the real coreos-pool URL when available vs synthesizing one).

review.summary: The PR replaces a workaround with a more aggressive approach: rewrite every non-coreos-pool URL into a synthesized koji canonical path. The logic is straightforward but has two notable risks: silent failure when arch parsing returns None (producing 'None' literally in the URL), and an acknowledged race condition with koji-tagger that has no mitigation or fallback. Minor concerns include duplicated arch lists and a regex that searches the full URL rather than path segments. Overall sound but worth tightening error handling before merge.
